source.title: UK Parliament demands unredacted METR safety report after Anthropic redacts most of the evidence
source.text: The UK Parliament is turning up the pressure on Anthropic. Committee chair Liam Byrne is demanding the unredacted METR safety report on AI acceleration by December 4. METR criticized Anthropic for cutting "most informative" evidence before publication. The episode raises broader questions about the transparency of voluntary AI safety evaluations and again shows Europe's dependence on US AI labs. The article UK Parliament demands unredacted METR safety report after Anthropic redacts most of the evidence appeared first on The Decoder .

draft.headline: UK Parliament orders Anthropic to reveal its redacted AI safety evidence.
draft.threads_post:
The UK Parliament is giving Anthropic until December 4 to hand over its full AI safety evidence. Committee chair Liam Byrne says the current version is missing the most informative data. Safety group METR criticized the lab for redacting key details from a report on AI acceleration. This demand highlights the limits of voluntary safety deals currently used by US-based labs.

Should AI labs be allowed to redact their own safety reports?

draft.instagram_caption:
The UK Parliament is giving Anthropic until December 4 to hand over its full AI safety evidence.

Committee chair Liam Byrne issued the demand after safety evaluator METR criticized Anthropic for cutting the "most informative" evidence from a public report. The document focused on AI acceleration, but the version released to the public was heavily redacted by the company.

This move shows the growing tension between government oversight and the voluntary safety checks used by major US AI labs.

Should AI labs be allowed to redact their own safety reports?
